# Capped phase-cell fusion outer (PR1673) on the T74 pivot-566+554 supplier

Conditional final kappa = **0.**. **What changed relative to PR1839, PR1875, PR1876 and PR1897: the supplier native and conservative complex endpoints are recertified to 1e-60000 (accept at the endpoint, reject at endpoint + 1e-60000) with the repaired even-term fine Mercator engine, the independent fine base-two engine and the exact-atanh oracle stage; the engines now evaluate in directed-rounding integer fixed point (monotone, floor for lower bounds and ceiling for upper bounds), which gives the same enclosure semantics as the exact-rational originals at a small fraction of the cost. Every free slack of the ledger is the fixed-grid-maximum point of PR2180 / PR2161 (dataisfire) at this package's own endpoint: r0, layout slack, q gap and endpoint gap 1e-60080, epsilon = 1 - (1025/1024) 1e-60080, beta = 1 - 3 (1025/1024) 1e-60080, zeta 1e-60082, stop 1e-60086, backoff 1e-60022, kappa floor grid 1e-60046. With C the certified complex endpoint, F the floor denominator and B the backoff, the ledger kappa is exactly C - 1/F - B, the maximum of the declared floor-grid/backoff family (every point has epsilon q < C and C F is an integer, so floor(F epsilon q)/F <= C - 1/F; attained since 0 < C - epsilon q < 1/F, checked exactly; `outer/PROOF-GRID-MAX.md`). The main-binding family condition (Gaussian saving minus main saving = delta (1 - 2q) > 0) is an explicit 63rd strict row `gaussian_above_main`; the 62 earlier strict inequalities and all 17 rejecting controls are retained. kappa exceeds PR2180 (dataisfire, 30000-digit endpoint) by 1.01065E-30002 and this package's previous 1e-60010-slack point by 2.00336E-60010. The single 60000-digit rejection moment of the strict assembly now uses the exact-integer coarse exponential of PR2168 (dataisfire; derivation as PR2184): `code/exact_coarse.py`, `EXACT-ARITHMETIC-DERIVATION.json`, intervals identical to the retained engine. Credit: dataisfire (#2161, #2180 fixed-grid maximum; #2168, #2184 exact-integer coarse exponential), Vlado Vojdanovski (#1673), chafreaky (#1786), Josie Elliston (#1956, the bootstrap-cutoff carry repair), M6LI (#1897), rohanarun (#1876, #1875, #1828 slack and endpoint refinements; #1319, #1297 supplier), chafreaky (#1786), Vlado Vojdanovski (#1673), mdumitrean (#1625), midhatn, philippeVV (#1519, the odd-term Mercator finding), Kothe and the existing lineage.** **Credit first: the fine source-prime padding is PR1786 (chafreaky / Chafik Boukhalfa), using Tim Trudgian's effective prime number theorem (vendored verbatim: `vendor/pr1786/FINE-PRIME-PADDING.md`); this package changes only its explicit parameter point (epsilon is free: epsilon = 1 - 1.0009765625e-60080, `outer/FINE-PADDING-COMPOSITION.md`) and combines it with this series' gauge-free interiors and radix-distributed union schedule, using the explicit Strassen boundary (the structured boundary of the previous package is no longer needed and not used).** The underlying construction is Vlado Vojdanovski's PR1673 (capped phase-cell fusion, its proof, PHASE-LAYOUT-AUDIT.md and exact evidence), on this repository's T74 supplier (PR1661's pivot-566 stack plus the pivot-554 kernel, certified complex endpoint 0.00167975495612554452133567...), with every free strict slack of PR1673 at 1e-60080 or below and b = certified endpoint - 1e-60080 (`outer/RETUNED-SLACKS.md`). Three changes are **new in this package series and not in PR1673 or PR1699** (the third, listed last, is new in this package): (1) the radix-distributed sparse-union schedule (`outer/UNION-SCHEDULE.md`, `outer/sched_test.py`, independent review simulation `outer/sched_review.py` by LeverRank), union row eps + 1/2 - xi instead of eps + beta + 1/2 - xi; (2) **structured boundary solves** (`outer/STRUCTURED-BOUNDARY.md`, executable exact check `outer/struct_check.py`): within a phase cell the Gaussian blocks factor exactly as D_r T D_c with T Toeplitz, the diagonals cancel through every Schur step, so every boundary segment block, coupling block, block-LU pivot and inverse pivot has constant displacement rank (proved bound 14, observed <= 4, flat in the segment index), is stored by Gohberg-Semencul / Kailath-Kung-Morf generators computed offline, and is applied by FFT in O(r W log W) ring operations per right-hand-side column, i.e. polylog per entry; the boundary row has exponent eps - xi + 1/2 + o(1), **tau_eff = 2 + 1e-60080** (tau_eff = 2 itself is not claimed; the polylog factors are absorbed by the strict slack). The boundary row and the union row now have the same exponent eps + 1/2 - xi and both bind together with main = fused Gaussian; the cap xi > 1/2 holds with margin 0.00084; kappa is +2.20e-7 over the previous package (rectangular k = 5, tau_eff = 2.1567081, outer/RECT-BOUNDARY.md, the documented fallback). The unproven omega_C <= 9/4 premise is not used. The union schedule and the structured boundary are new constructions that require independent review; the structured argument's precision section (STRUCTURED-BOUNDARY.md section 5) is an error argument from PR1673's audited bounds, not a verified stability theorem, and the real-regime check at large p has not been run. Conditional on all inherited hypotheses. (3) **gauge-free interiors** (`outer/GAUGEFREE-INTERIORS.md`, executable `outer/check_gaugefree.py`): the linear part of the local gauge is exactly a fractional centre shift of the Toeplitz kernel (broad and narrow, exact identities); the shifted Gaussian symbol is accretive (Jacobi triple product, Re phi >= mu = poly(p)^-1 on the unit circle), so SHALLOW-TOEPLITZ sec. 9 extends from SPD to accretive Toeplitz tiles; only the quadratic chirp remains (range O(a B^2/d)), the precision guard becomes beta + 2 xi - eps <= 1 - r - zeta, and the union tag check becomes 1 - beta > 0 (tag work is paid per visit). beta = 0.9966, xi = 0.5017, eps = 0.9999944.

The supplier's own strict-assembly kappa, recorded in `CLAIM.json` and `new/SPEC.json` (unchanged by the outer retune), is 0..

**Margins are asymptotic.** *(Inherited pkg8-era figures, superseded by the paragraph below, which gives the current point epsilon = 1 - 1.0009765625e-60080, beta = 1 - 3.0029296875e-60080; the numbers in this paragraph describe the earlier package.)* The earlier parameters sat close to several walls: 1 - beta = 3.35e-3 (record header g log L, tag work per visit, support g polylog p = o(p)), membership 1 - beta - 2(1-eps) = 3.34e-3, 1 - eps = 5.6e-6, cap xi - 1/2 = 1.67e-3, and the global router margin is only 9.4e-9. Every claim of the form 'polylog p is o(p^margin)' holds only for sufficiently large p and rests on the strict 1e-60080 slacks; this is the same status as the earlier packages' margins, but with much smaller exponents.

**Margins are asymptotic, and now with exponent margin 1.0009765625e-60080** (1 - epsilon = 1.0009765625e-60080, 1 - beta = 3.0029296875e-60080, membership gap 1.0009765625e-60080): every 'eventually' of the proofs needs p beyond an astronomically large cutoff; no practical cutoff is claimed. Epsilon < 1 strictly and kappa < q always.

Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.14.0 is only needed for the vendored PR1673 evidence checks that import it.

kappa = 0.001676938111022438771190100017020725032555691674761792047536039179. `new/CHAIN.json` lists every kernel step; `new/rebuild_chain.py` re-verifies each step against its own base words (exact B + early-cleanup map over all rows, remaining cleanup, interfaces). # PR1625's pivot-566 helper-donor kernel on the T74 exact fill, with certified 1e-60000 endpoints and a 1e-59995 outer witness

## Credit and lineage
The construction gain is PR1625 (mdumitrean): a seven-insert helper-donor kernel for cold pivot 566 on the two local words of PR1297, as vendored in PR1319 (H1 +1, H2 -2, H3 +1 per call on both words; owners, dispatch, parent and idle remainder reused byte-for-byte). `new/gauge44-word-566.json.gz`, `new/extra-word-566.json.gz`, `new/EDITS.json`, `new/rebuild.py`, `new/rebind.py` and the rebound `new/PLAN.json`/`new/PROFILE.json` are PR1625's. The T74 construction is PR1319 (rohanarun) over PR1297's four cold kernels (rohanarun; kernel 531 PR1274 jeremykothe2, kernel 543 PR1286 rohanarun). The outer-witness / endpoint refinement lineage: PR1424, PR1485, PR1574 (rohanarun); PR1479, PR1510, PR1513, PR1536, PR1578 (jeremykothe2); PR1534, PR1549 (midhatn); the soundness repair of the fine Mercator engine is PR1519 (philippeVV); PR1625's own 1e-200 stack is the baseline compared against.

## What this package adds on top of PR1625
1. Certified complex endpoints (native and conservative, recomputed for the new global profile) at 1e-60000: the retained engines certify the inherited 1e-24 bracket containing each endpoint, and finer-constant copies of both engines (`code/fine_mercator.py`: 2^-199536 outward rounding, 199536 (even) Mercator terms, 30042 exponential terms; `code/fine_moment.py`: 2^-199593 outward rounding, 62962 log terms, 30042 exponential terms; both evaluate in directed-rounding integer fixed point, floor for lower bounds and ceiling for upper bounds) certify accept at the endpoint and reject at endpoint + 1e-60000, both required. Repaired engine (even term count, asserted) plus the independent exact atanh oracle stage (`code/oracle_check.py`, stage `fine-engine-oracle`).
2. Outer witness settings in `new/SPEC.json:outer_refinement`: grid_digits 59995 (the final kappa grid), margin_digits 60005 (eta = beta = 10^-60005), bootstrap_steps 22228, endpoint_digits 60000; `dec()` prints 60120 significant digits. The bootstrap chain is evaluated in exact integers on a 2^-240084 grid: the internal parameter s is replaced by its floor on the grid and every exponent is rounded down (a smaller exponent or parameter only weakens the bootstrap; the difference is far below the kappa grid), every strict condition is checked exactly, and every stage's cutoff carries the previous constant: with ell_j >= log2 C_j, stage j needs L_j*gap_j^2 >= 36 and L_j*gap_j >= 2(4+ell_j), and the next constant is C_large + C_old*2^(L_j*(a_{j+1}-a_j)) (PR387 PROOF, FINITE_BIT_ACCOUNTING.md), i.e. ell_{j+1} = max(512, ell_j + ceil(L_j*(a_{j+1}-a_j))) + 1; L_j is the least power of two (up to one doubling) meeting both inequalities, both are asserted exactly in integers at proof time for every stage of both branches, and a control asserts that the uncarried cutoffs max(ceil(36/gap^2), ceil(2(4+512)/gap)) of the earlier lineage FAIL the carry rule from stage 2 on (finding of PR1956, Josie Elliston; repair (a)). kappa is unchanged (it is computed from the chain end only). `ASSEMBLY.json` records per-step SHA-256 digests of the exponent, gap and log2 C bound, the cutoff exponent and the carry size instead of the full values.
3. `verify.py` additionally: rebuilds both shipped words from PR1297's pinned words (`new/rebuild.py`), runs the retained `audit_local.py` on them, runs the lineage native chain on both (or reuses hash-checked cached natives), rebinds the PLAN (`new/rebind.py`, must equal `new/PLAN.json` beyond bind-rebound receipt hashes), then the strict T74 chain on `new/PLAN.json` and `new/SPEC.json`; the fine-engine results are memoised across stages (`code/fine_cache.py`, keyed by engine hash and arguments).

4. Stage `lemmag-labels` (beside the frame-only `local-replay`; `code/lemmag_stage.py` with `code/lemmag_checks.py`, vendored verbatim from PR1964 by thakrarsagar / Sagar Thakrar; Lemma G by DreamingOfClouds, PR509 / PR516): runs the Lemma G extended-label check (`label_check`, strict and permissive readings) and the adapter rule (`adapter_rule`) on each provider's emitted LOCAL-PROGRAMS in both orientations, asserting 0 violations, and requires the three physically wrong adapter mutants that the frame-only replay accepts (X exit straddle, Y entry straddle, Z exit adapters moved before a phase-B add) to be REJECTED on every provider.

The top-level PLAN.json/SPEC.json are the unchanged PR1424/PR1319 files used by the owner reconstruction and parent lift checks; the strict stage uses `new/`. All 47 strict outer inequalities, the rejection controls and next-grid rejection hold (checked offline with the package's own outer witness and engine). The remaining gap to the exact root is the 1e-60000 endpoint bracket; the displayed digits are set by the 1e-59995 grid.

The three witness settings are frozen in `SPEC.json:outer_refinement`: 12 bootstrap iterations, eta = beta = 10^-40 with target backoff 10^-43, and a 10^-36 final κ grid. The inherited complex and bit endpoint grids and their native/surcharge models remain unchanged. Every bootstrap cutoff is recomputed from the exact gap. The next final κ grid point rejects for this witness. No optimality over all outer parameters is claimed.

The recurrence is a_(j+1) = (1-s)s + s a_j. Its closed form is a_j = s - (s-a_0)s^j; 0 < a_0 < s < 1 gives a finite increasing chain below s. This only changes witnesses to the inherited conditional bootstrap and outer lemmas, whose assumptions remain in force. Root endpoints, arithmetic engines and finite construction are inherited unchanged.

Reproduce complete admission with `python3 -B verify.py --work /absolute/new/work --base-native-from /bound/base/native --extra-native-from /bound/extra/native`, or omit the two reuse flags for fresh native supplier runs. The output directory must not exist and assertions must be enabled. `evidence/OUTER-DISCOVERY.json` is discovery evidence, not a completed new-package replay. `evidence/pr1377/` contains predecessor receipts; inherited `PRICE.json` and input/parent receipts are not new verification.

Conditional finite construction only. All-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, exact recovery, analytic transfer, PR559 recurrence correction and PR589 bit H1-H5 assumptions remain. No unconditional theorem, full Lean certification, or global packing claim.
